attacks.claim: The upstream 429 retry never passes through the tenant bucket, so a tenant can generate up to about 2x its configured upstream calls during an upstream 429 storm. The amplification is bounded to one retry per admitted request. The sleep is also not tied to the client abort signal, and the retry path has no route-level tests.
attacks.evidence:
await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, delay));
      res = await upstream.chat(req.body, { signal: req.signal });

attacks.claim: ratePerSec of 0 is not validated, so waitMs becomes Infinity and the Retry-After header is the string "Infinity". An HTTP-date Retry-After also silently falls back to 1s.

The log line carries a truncated unsalted SHA-256 of the API key. It is not the key and tenant.id is already logged, so it adds little. A keyed HMAC, or dropping the field, would be more conservative given the rule that keys never appear in logs.
There is no config kill switch for the limiter, so rolling back a bad default requires a redeploy. The default of 20 rps / burst 40 applies to tenants without explicit limits.
attacks.evidence: limits from tenant config, default 20 rps / burst 40
